order: Kim Min-jae likely to sit out Uzbekistan friendly after missing training for second straight day
Korea’s dominating defender, Kim Min-jae, is unlikely to play in Tuesday’s friendly against Uzbekistan after missing team training for a second consecutive day.

With Kim showing signs of physical and mental fatigue, he is likely to sit out the Uzbekistan match. Defender Kim Tae-hyeon of Kashima Antlers, who represented the players at Monday’s press conference, is likely to start alongside Lee Han-beom of Club Brugge.

“Kim has undergone separate recovery training for two straight days,” a national team representative said. “It’s not a serious injury that would require him to leave the squad. He seems to be dealing with fatigue from his recent matches.”

The Bayern Munich center half sat out the national team’s training session at Korea Football Park in Cheonan, South Chungcheong, on Monday, a day before the friendly against Uzbekistan at Yongin Mireu Stadium in Gyeonggi. He instead trained separately indoors.
The imposing center back, who expressed frustration with the side after the 0-0 draw with Venezuela, is dealing with fatigue, a team representative said.

Moreno, whose status as permanent manager will be decided after the friendly against Uzbekistan and two more matches through November, said he would not use the limited time available to him as an excuse.

Kim Min-jae was not the only player to voice frustration after the Venezuela match. Midfielder Hwang In-beom of Porto became emotional as he pointed to the vacancy at the top of the Korea Football Association and the national team’s interim coaching setup.
